answer: Spectral neighborhood gating. Each agent’s transactions are weighted by the diversity of its counterparties’ recent graph positions; a cluster of fresh identities echoing one another collapses to a narrow spectrum. Only agents whose flow spans many disjoint neighborhoods, like a river fed by scattered tributaries, clear the threshold. An attacker must sustain varied, organic counterparties per identity — a walnut of real activity, not a shell — and each fake identity costs ongoing graph-diverse traffic, not one payment. A raven hopping between isolated nodes can’t fake that span cheaply.
